newsitem.title: CHINA: China says conflict with U.S. unlikely.
newsitem.headline: China says conflict with U.S. unlikely.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Friday conflict between China and the United States was not possible unless Washington infringed on Beijing's sovereignty or territorial integrity.

"There is no possibility for China and the United States to enter into conflict with each other unless the United States harbours a desire to infringe upon China's sovereignty and territorial integrity," Qian told reporters.
Qian was asked to comment on suggestions that despite a current improvement in relations between China and the United States, the two countries would one day be adversaries.
He described the suggestions as stemming from the "China threat theory", a school of thought that maintains China's growing economic and military strength are a threat to the region and the world.
Qian, who is also a vice-premier, did not elaborate on what might constitute an infringement of China's sovereignty but he expected Sino-U.S. ties to grow in future due to common interests.
China's policy towards the the United States was to enhance trust, reduce difficulties, develop cooperation and avoid confrontation, he said.
Sino-U.S. relations have improved gradually in recent months after plunging over Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's private, landmark trip to the United States in June 1995.

Tension between the United States and China was high when Washington sent warships near Taiwan in a show of force in March last year. That followed Beijing's war games and missile tests near Taiwan aimed at intimidating the island.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province, has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation and has threatened to use force if Taipei authorities declare independence.
China and the United States have been painstakingly restoring their damaged ties in recent months.
Vice-President Al Gore is expected to visit China later this month as part of a series of senior level meetings expected to culminate with an exchange of presidential visits.
